description.narrative: The expected impacts are likely to center around: Strengthen downstream linkages: Kirene distributes its products through about SME wholesalers and semi-wholesalers in Senegal, which it actively supports with its own sales team and promotional / marketing materials. Economy-wide effects: By increasing production capacity, the Project will create direct and indirect jobs, as well as incremental value added. Consumers: Consumption of sugar-dense beverages (both CSD and juices) is associated with the negative nutritional outcomes for the consumers. The impacts could be mitigated by exploring reformulation or shifting production towards healthier choices. Environment: The project will promote recycling and, hence reduce the related carbon footprint and plastic waste. Kirene will promote recycling, hence reducing the related carbon footprint and waste. There may be scope for market impacts along this dimension in the FMCG market in Senegal.

The proposed loan of up to 8.3 million (the IFC Loan) to SIAGRO S.A. (the Company, the Borrower or Kirene), a still and carbonated soft drinks (CSD) processing company, is to support the Borrowers investment program and includes: (i) expanding production capacity; (ii) Green building standards and certification, and (iv) working capital requirements. The project is expected to be supported by the Canada-IFC Blended Climate Finance Program (BCFP), as described in the Blended Finance Section.
